quizzes.title: PVTGs and PM-JANMAN: Practice Quiz
quizzes.passage: Great Nicobar Island is the southernmost island of India and also the largest of the Nicobar Islands. Most of the island is covered by tropical rainforest, and its coastal areas include Galathea Bay and Campbell Bay. Several indigenous communities live on the island, including the Shompen, the Nicobarese, the Andamanese and the Onge. The island is home to the Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve, and Indira Point marks the southernmost point of India. The Great Nicobar Mega Infrastructure Project proposes an international container transshipment terminal, a gas and solar based power plant, a dual-use civil-military airport and an integrated township. The island is strategically placed near the Malacca Strait, which is one reason the project is described as important for India's Act East Policy. The project has raised concerns about its effects on the island. Among the communities named in these concerns are the Shompen and the Nicobarese. The concerns include loss of habitat, cultural disruption and the impact on livelihoods. The island also lies in the highest seismic risk zone, which makes it vulnerable to earthquakes, tsunamis and climate change. The National Green Tribunal, which upheld the environmental clearance for the project, noted that the project complied with the Island Coastal Regulation Zone and Coastal Regulation Zone norms. The project is being implemented by the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Integrated Development Corporation.

questions.q: Which body has identified the Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups?
options: Andaman and Nicobar Islands Integrated Development Corporation
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs has identified the PVTGs.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT listed among the facilities that PM-JANMAN aims to provide to PVTG families?
options: 450 MVA gas and solar-based power plant
questions.explanation: Safe housing, water and sanitation, health and nutrition, and road and telecom connectivity are PM-JANMAN facilities, while the 450 MVA power plant is a component of the wider Great Nicobar project.

questions.q: What is the outlay of PM-JANMAN?
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the outlay of PM-JANMAN as Rs. 24,000 crore.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups are considered to have a subsistence economy.
Reason (R): They face challenging living conditions.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both are listed as salient features, but the booklet does not link the living conditions to the economy.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Former name of PVTGs   ->   A. Primitive Tribal Groups
II. Larger category of which PVTG is a sub-classification   ->   B. Scheduled Tribe
III. Aim of PM-JANMAN   ->   C. Holistic development of PVTGs
IV. Commission that set up the PTG category in 1973   ->   D. Dhebar Commission
questions.explanation: PVTGs were previously Primitive Tribal Groups, are a sub-classification of Scheduled Tribe, PM-JANMAN aims at holistic development, and the Dhebar Commission set up the PTG category in 1973.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the salient features of PVTGs:
I. Technological backwardness is one of their salient features.
II. Their population growth is described as steadily increasing.
III. Low literacy levels are among their salient features.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Technological backwardness and low literacy are listed features, whereas the booklet describes population growth as stagnant or declining.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements are correct?
I. A PVTG is considered more vulnerable than a regular Scheduled Tribe.
II. PM-JANMAN has an outlay of Rs. 2,400 crore.
III. PM-JANMAN covers health and nutrition.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the outlay in statement II is Rs. 24,000 crore, not Rs. 2,400 crore.

quizzes.title: PVTGs and PM-JANMAN: Short Answer
quizzes.passage: Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups, known as PVTGs, are communities considered more vulnerable than other tribal groups in India. A national scheme aims at their overall development and at improving their socio-economic conditions. The scheme's support is meant for PVTG families, who face challenging living conditions. The Shompen are one such group, and they live on Great Nicobar Island, the southernmost island of India. The island is largely covered by tropical rainforest, and its coastal areas include Galathea Bay and Campbell Bay. The Nicobarese, the Andamanese and the Onge also live on the island. The Great Nicobar Mega Infrastructure Project has raised concerns about the Shompen and the Nicobarese. These concerns include loss of habitat, cultural disruption and the impact on livelihoods. The island also lies in the highest seismic risk zone, so it is vulnerable to earthquakes and tsunamis. The island is home to the Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve, and Indira Point marks the southernmost point of India. The project includes an international container transshipment terminal, a gas and solar based power plant, a dual-use civil-military airport and an integrated township. The project is being implemented by the Andaman and Nicobar Islands Integrated Development Corporation, and the National Green Tribunal has upheld its environmental clearance, citing compliance with coastal regulation norms.

questions.q: In which year did the Dhebar Commission set up the PTG category? (give the year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Dhebar Commission established the Primitive Tribal Group category in 1973.

questions.q: A PVTG is a sub-classification of which larger category? (name it in two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet defines a PVTG as a sub-classification of Scheduled Tribe or a section of one.

questions.q: Which national scheme for PVTGs has an outlay of Rs. 24,000 crore? (give the acronym)
questions.explanation: The booklet gives the outlay of PM-JANMAN as Rs. 24,000 crore.

questions.q: One salient feature of PVTGs is population growth that is stagnant or ___. Which word fills the blank? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists stagnant or declining population growth among the salient features of PVTGs.

questions.q: The PM-JANMAN scheme covers road and ___ connectivity. Which word fills the blank? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet lists road and telecom connectivity among the facilities covered by PM-JANMAN.

questions.q: Which ministry has identified the PVTGs? (name the ministry)
accept: Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the Ministry of Tribal Affairs has identified 75 PVTGs across 18 states and one Union Territory.

questions.q: The scheme's aim is the ___ development of PVTGs. Which word fills the blank? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says PM-JANMAN is aimed at the holistic development of PVTGs and improving their socio-economic conditions.

quizzes.title: National Green Tribunal: Practice Quiz
quizzes.passage: The National Green Tribunal is a specialised tribunal that hears environmental disputes in India. Its work includes giving relief and compensation for environmental damage, and its approach is based on sustainable development. The Tribunal has regional benches in cities such as Bhopal, Pune and Chennai, and it is headed by a Chairperson along with judicial members. Environmental disputes can involve pollution, forests and water. The Tribunal provides a dedicated forum for such matters. In a recent decision, the Tribunal upheld the environmental clearance granted to the Great Nicobar Mega Infrastructure Project. It found that the project complied with the Island Coastal Regulation Zone and Coastal Regulation Zone norms. The project includes an international container transshipment terminal, a gas and solar based power plant, a dual-use civil-military airport and an integrated township. It is intended to reduce India's reliance on the ports of Singapore and Colombo. The project has also raised environmental concerns, including the diversion of tropical rainforest and the loss of a large number of trees. The island also lies in the highest seismic risk zone, so it is vulnerable to earthquakes, tsunamis and climate change. The island is home to the Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve. Indira Point marks the southernmost point of India.

questions.q: Which of the following Acts is excluded from the civil jurisdiction of the National Green Tribunal?
options: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act 1981
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Tribunal's civil jurisdiction excludes the Wildlife Protection Act 1972 and the Forest Rights Act 2006.

questions.q: The Tribunal's work on relief and compensation for environmental damage is linked to which principle?
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the polluter pays principle alongside relief, compensation and sustainable development.

questions.q: After which two countries did India become the third country to set up a specialised environmental tribunal?
questions.explanation: The booklet says India is the third country after Australia and New Zealand to set up a specialised environmental tribunal.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Appeals against the Tribunal's decisions lie with the High Court within 90 days.
Reason (R): Appeals against the Tribunal's decisions can be filed in the Supreme Court within 90 days.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The booklet says appeals go to the Supreme Court within 90 days, so the High Court statement is wrong while the reason is right.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. National Green Tribunal Act   ->   A. Enacted in 2010
II. Appeals to the Supreme Court must be filed within   ->   B. 90 days
III. Appeals must be disposed of within   ->   C. 6 months
IV. Wildlife Protection Act   ->   D. Enacted in 1972
questions.explanation: The booklet links the NGT Act to 2010, appeals to 90 days, disposal of appeals to 6 months, and the Wildlife Protection Act to 1972.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Tribunal:
I. The exact number of judicial members is decided by the Central Government.
II. Decisions of the Tribunal cannot be challenged in any court.
III. The Tribunal is bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I matches the booklet, since appeals lie to the Supreme Court and the Tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the National Green Tribunal are correct?
I. It hears civil cases under seven laws.
II. Appeals against its decisions go to the High Court.
III. Its decisions can be executed as a decree of a civil court.
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while statement II is wrong because appeals go to the Supreme Court.

Its civil jurisdiction covers a number of environmental laws, although some Acts are kept outside its scope. The island is home to the Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve, and Indira Point marks the southernmost point of India. questions.q: In which year was the National Green Tribunal Act passed? (give the year)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Tribunal was set up under the National Green Tribunal Act (2010).

questions.q: Within how many days can an appeal against a Tribunal decision be filed in the Supreme Court? (give the number of days)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that appeals can be filed in the Supreme Court within 90 days.

questions.q: Within how many months must the Tribunal dispose of appeals? (give the number of months)
questions.explanation: The booklet says appeals must be disposed of within 6 months of filing.

questions.q: Name the principle, applied by the Tribunal, under which the party causing environmental damage is made to pay (three words).
questions.explanation: The booklet lists the polluter pays principle as one of the Tribunal's guiding approaches.

questions.q: Which Act excluded from the Tribunal's civil jurisdiction dates from 2006? (name it in two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Forest Rights Act 2006 is excluded from the Tribunal's civil jurisdiction.

questions.q: Which authority decides the exact number of judicial members of the Tribunal? (name it in two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet states that the exact number of judicial members is decided by the Central Government.

questions.q: Which Act excluded from the Tribunal's civil jurisdiction dates from 1972? (name it in two words)
questions.explanation: The booklet says the Wildlife Protection Act 1972 is excluded from the Tribunal's civil jurisdiction.
